text: On 14 January 2019, a Boeing 707-3J9C, serial number 21128 and registered as EP-CPP, operated by Saha Airlines on a cargo flight crashed at Fath Air Base, near Karaj, Alborz province, Iran. This aircraft was the last civil Boeing 707 in operation. It was owned by the Islamic Republic of Iran Air Force (IRIAF) and had been leased to Saha Airlines. The aircraft was 42 years old at the time of the accident, having first flown on 19 November 1976 and been delivered to the Imperial Iranian Air Force as 5–8312. It was transferred to Saha Airlines on 27 February 2000, re-registered as EP-SHK, and subsequently returned to the IRIAF in December 2015 before being re-leased to Saha Airlines in May 2016 with the registration EP-CPP. The aircraft had suffered substantial damage from an uncontained engine failure on 3 August 2009 during a flight from Ahvaz International Airport to Mehrabad International Airport, Tehran, leading to an emergency landing at Ahvaz, after which it was repaired. The flight was intended to carry meat from Manas International Airport in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, to Payam International Airport in Karaj, Iran, but the crew mistakenly landed at Fath Air Base, likely confusing its shorter runway with the longer Payam runway, as the two are only a few kilometres apart and aligned similarly. A Boeing 707 typically requires a runway longer than 2,500 meters (8,200 feet), but Fath Air Base's runway is only 1,300 meters (4,300 feet). Poor weather conditions were also reported. The aircraft overran the runway, crashed through a wall, and collided with a house in the Farrokhabad neighborhood of Fardis County, Alborz province. Security footage captured the crash and subsequent fire. The houses were unoccupied at the time, and no ground injuries occurred. Fifteen of the sixteen crew members on board died; one, flight engineer Farshad Mahdavinejad, survived but was seriously injured and taken to Shariati Hospital in critical condition. There were no passengers. Early reports indicated either 16 or 17 people on board, all but one of whom died. An investigation was launched, and the cockpit voice recorder, flight data recorder, and control display unit were recovered from the wreckage on 14 January.
